romans-10-study-notes.summary: Israel was rejected due to not feeling a need for salvation, making their own traditions, being proud, and misunderstanding the law.
key_points: Did not feel need for salvation; thought they were fine.
Made own traditions and worshipped them.
Proud and self-righteous; refused to listen and learn.
Misunderstood the law; it leads the sinner to the savior.
sections: Israel rejections — Reasons for their rejection 1-13

related.title: Remedy for Rejection
related.why: This note explains the necessary steps, like hearing the message first, to counteract the reasons Israel was rejected.

related.title: Results of Rejection
related.why: This note addresses the consequence of Israel's rejection, contrasting their actions with God's continued desire for His people.

related.title: Foundation of Dedication
related.why: This note connects the theological truths about condemnation and justification to the dedication of the believer, which is a core element of the rejection discussion.

romans-10-study-notes.summary: The remedy involves a missionary program, emphasizing that believing and obeying are not interchangeable, and that one must first hear.
key_points: Used for missionary program.
Believing and obeying are not interchangeable.
To believe one must first hear.
sections: Remedy for Rejection 14-17

related.title: Reasons for Rejection
related.why: This note explains the root causes of rejection, which helps contextualize why the missionary program (Remedy for Rejection) is necessary.

related.title: Results of Rejection
related.why: This note contrasts the failure of Israel with the ongoing yearning of God, providing the motivation behind the need for the missionary program.

related.title: Foundation of Dedication
related.why: This note establishes the theological groundwork (condemnation, justification, assurance) upon which the dedication required by the remedy is built.

romans-10-study-notes.summary: Israel is guilty because they did hear, and the message is shared with Gentiles, yet God still yearns for His people.
key_points: Israel is guilty; they DID hear.
Message is shared with Gentiles due to Israel rejection.
God still yearns for His people.
sections: Results of their rejection 18-21

related.title: Reasons for Rejection
related.why: This note explains the specific reasons why Israel faced rejection, which provides the context for the general summary.

related.why: This note details the practical steps and emphasis needed to overcome the rejection described in the summary.

related.title: Foundation of Dedication
related.why: This note connects the concept of dedication to the theological truths that underpin the believer's response to rejection.

romans-12-study-notes.summary: The dedication of the believer is based on the preceding theological truths regarding condemnation, justification, and assurance, which serve as the basis for the dedication described in Romans 12:1.
key_points: Romans 3:20 is the 'therefore' of condemnation.
Romans 5:1 is the 'therefore' of justification.
Romans 8:1 is the 'therefore' of assurance.
Romans 12:1 is the 'therefore' of dedication.
sections: Romans 12 has the fourth “therefore” in Romans

related.title: Living Sacrifice
related.why: This note provides the practical application of dedication by illustrating how the body, mind, and will are offered as sacrifices.

related.title: Mind as Sacrifice
related.why: This note explains the internal mechanism of dedication by showing how the mind is transformed through the Holy Spirit.

related.title: Will as Sacrifice
related.why: This note details the active component of dedication by showing how surrendering the will enables God's power to take over.

romans-12-study-notes.summary: The body is a living sacrifice requiring two examples: Isaac, who died in obedience, and Jesus Christ, who died in sacrifice.
key_points: Your body is a living sacrifice to give to God.
Isaac died in obedience to God.
Jesus Christ actually died in sacrifice.
sections: Dedication - 3 steps > Your body is a living sacrifice to give to God

related.title: Mind as Sacrifice
related.why: This note explains how the mind is a sacrifice by detailing how the Holy Spirit transforms thinking into genuine change.

related.title: Will as Sacrifice
related.why: This note connects the concept of the living sacrifice to the practical act of surrendering one's will to God through prayer.

related.title: Foundation of Dedication
related.why: This note establishes the theological groundwork that supports the believer's dedication as a living sacrifice.

romans-12-study-notes.summary: The mind is a sacrifice because the Holy Spirit changes thinking by releasing inner power, leading to transformation rather than mere conformity.
key_points: The world wants to change your mind with external pressure.
The Holy Spirit changes your mind by releasing power within.
If God controls your thinking, you are a transformer.
sections: Dedication - 3 steps > Your mind is a sacrifice to God

related.title: Will as Sacrifice
related.why: This note explains how surrendering the will to God through disciplined prayer is a mechanism by which His power takes over, which is closely related to how the mind is transformed by the Holy Spirit.

related.title: Living Sacrifice
related.why: This note provides a concrete example (Isaac and Jesus) of what it means to offer one's entire being—including the mind—as a sacrifice.

related.title: God's Sovereignty
related.why: Understanding God's perfect plan and sovereignty provides the ultimate context for why the mind is changed by the Holy Spirit, as it is part of His overarching purpose.

romans-12-study-notes.summary: The will is a sacrifice because surrendering it to God allows His power to take over, which is achieved through disciplined prayer.
key_points: Your mind controls your body, your will controls your mind.
Yielding our will to God gives us willpower.
Surrender happens through disciplined prayer.
Pray about EVERYTHING and yield plans to Him.
sections: Dedication - 3 steps > Your will is a sacrifice to God

related.title: Living Sacrifice
related.why: This note provides a concrete example of what a living sacrifice entails, contrasting the abstract concept of the will as a sacrifice with the practical reality of the body as a sacrifice.

related.title: Mind as Sacrifice
related.why: This note explains how the mind is transformed by the Holy Spirit, which is the mechanism through which surrendering the will to God leads to change.

related.title: Foundation of Dedication
related.why: This note establishes the theological groundwork (condemnation, justification, assurance) upon which the dedication of the believer, including the surrender of the will, is built.

romans-12-study-notes.summary: Christian relationships involve honest self-evaluation of gifts, faithful cooperation regardless of personal feelings, and loving participation through patience and sharing burdens.
key_points: Each Christian must identify spiritual gifts and ministry.
Be honest in evaluation; neither under nor over-evaluating is pride.
Work with others even if you don't like them.
Gifts are tools to build with, not weapons to fight with.
Love is the circulatory system of the spiritual body.
Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, and faithful in prayer.
Share the burdens of others.
sections: Relationship (to other believers) > Faithful cooperation
Relationship (to other believers) > Honest evaluation
Relationship (to other believers) > Loving participation

related.title: Love in Dealing with Enemies
related.why: This note directly addresses how to apply the principle of loving participation and patience in relationships when facing conflict.

romans-12-study-notes.summary: Returning good for evil requires love, which distinguishes following Christ from being impatient and lacking love toward enemies.
key_points: Returning good for evil requires love.
Having enemies shows impatience and lack of love.
Following Christ is different from having enemies.
Justice should be viewed as love.
sections: Relationship (to enemies)

related.title: Relationship to Others
related.why: This note directly addresses how to handle relationships, including loving others even when dealing with enemies.

related.title: Viewing Revenge and Justice
related.why: This note provides a framework for viewing revenge, which is a key component in deciding how to respond to enemies.

related.title: God's Sovereignty
related.why: Understanding God's sovereignty helps frame the context for loving enemies by recognizing His ultimate plan.

romans-12-study-notes.summary: The study examines how to view revenge by considering whether one positions oneself as better or less deserving of justice than others, and whether justice is viewed as love.
key_points: Consider how to view revenge.
Examine if one positions self as better/less deserving of justice.
Examine if justice is viewed as love.
sections: Relationship (to enemies)

related.title: Love in Dealing with Enemies
related.why: This note directly addresses how to view the response to wrongdoing, which is central to the concept of justice and revenge.

related.title: Relationship to Others
related.why: This note provides the framework for how believers interact with others, which informs the ethical basis for viewing justice.

related.title: God's Sovereignty
related.why: Understanding God's ultimate plan provides a theological context for how human concepts of justice and revenge fit into the larger divine order.

romans-08-study-notes.summary: Romans 8 outlines four spiritual freedoms: freedom from judgment, freedom from defeat, freedom from discouragement, and freedom from separation.
key_points: Freedom from judgment (No condemnation).
Freedom from defeat (No obligation; submit to God).
Freedom from discouragement (No frustration).
Freedom from separation.
sections: Commentary Used: Wiersbe commentary — Romans 8 covers four spiritual freedoms:

related.title: Foundation of Dedication
related.why: This note explains the theological groundwork that underpins the believer's freedom from judgment and defeat.

related.title: Hope and Assurance
related.why: This note connects the freedom from discouragement and separation to the ultimate assurance of adoption.

romans-08-study-notes.summary: Suffering is a result of Adam’s sin, but it is not useless; creation groans, believers groan, and the Holy Spirit groans, yet God has a perfect plan.
key_points: Creation groans (18-22): Suffering is a result of Adam’s sin but is not useless; pain leads to something beautiful and ends.
Believers groan (23-25): Believers have a taste of glory to come but are anxious to get there.
Holy Spirit groans (23-30): The Spirit groans but also prays on our behalf.
God is always at work (28) and has a perfect plan (29) for those who love Him and are called according to His purpose.
sections: Romans 8:18-30 discusses suffering and pain, and how we are now free from discouragement > Three groans are mentioned > Believers groan (23-25)

romans-08-study-notes.summary: Believers have hope because they know the climax of adoption is coming, and faith is the assurance of things hoped for.
key_points: Believers have a taste of glory to come but are anxious to get there.
Adoption is the redemption of the body when Jesus comes back, with a 'climax' at the Rapture.
We as believers still have hope as we know the climax of that adoption is coming.
Faith is the assurance of things hoped for and the conviction of things not seen.
